reference: Hosking & Wallis, Regional Frequency Analysis (1997), appendix A.8; C# literals verified against the R lmom package
comment: Every value below is a literal lifted from the C# test file named in `source`. The C# test's Test_ParametersToString case has no C++ counterpart (ParametersToString / GetParameterPropertyNames / MinimumOfParameters / MaximumOfParameters are WPF-facing and unported across this whole distribution layer), and its Test_Moments and Test_GNO_PartialDerivatives cases assert only self-consistency (Mean/StandardDeviation/Skewness/Kurtosis against CentralMoments(1E-8); QuantileGradient against the same NumericalDerivative.Gradient call it makes internally) rather than any literal, so neither is carried as a literal here. Those three surfaces -- product moments, seeded draws, and QuantileGradient -- are instead pinned from the real C# library through the dotnet oracle gate; each such assertion carries its own `source` field. ParameterCovariance and QuantileVariance are deliberately absent: upstream throws NotImplementedException for both (GeneralizedNormal.cs 509 and 515) and the port mirrors the throw, so there is no value to reproduce.

cases.name: lmom_fit_air_quality_wind
cases.comment: Test_GNO_LMOM: method-of-L-moments fit to R's air-quality wind series, then the forward L-moment map off the fitted parameters. Tolerances are the C# test's own 0.0001 absolute.

cases.name: dist_lmom_fit_air_quality_wind
cases.comment: Test_GNO_Dist: PDF/CDF at 14.9 off the same L-moment fit, plus the CDF->InverseCDF round trip. C# asserts InverseCDF(gno.CDF(14.9)) == 14.9; here the quantile is evaluated at the CDF LITERAL (0.912294, good to 5e-7), so the same 0.0001 absolute tolerance the C# test uses covers the literal's own rounding (dx ~ dp/pdf ~ 1.3e-5).

cases.name: cdf_xi97_alpha35_kappa_neg01
cases.comment: Test_GNO_CDF: GeneralizedNormal(9.7, 3.5, -0.1) verified against the R lmom package, at the C# test's own 1E-7 tolerance.

cases.name: inverse_cdf_round_trip_xi97_alpha35_kappa_neg01
cases.comment: Second half of Test_GNO_CDF: InverseCDF(CDF(x)) == x. C# feeds back the freshly computed CDF; here the quantile is evaluated at the CDF literals above, which the C# test itself pins only to its own 1E-7 absolute tolerance. An error dp in the probability maps to dx = dp / pdf(x), and the loosest of the five points is x = 18, where pdf(18) = 0.009567: a 1E-7 pin therefore admits dx = 1.0e-5, which is the order 1e-05 covers. (The literals as written carry only their own 8-decimal 5e-9 rounding, so the round trip actually lands within ~5e-7; 1e-05 is the bound the pin justifies, not the observed error. The C# 1E-7 applies to the un-rounded round trip, not to this one.)

cases.name: construction_default
cases.comment: Test_Construction: the default constructor is SetParameters(100, 10, 0), which is exactly what this construct performs.

cases.name: construction_negative_location
cases.comment: Test_Construction: GeneralizedNormal(-100, 1, 1). kappa=1 > NearZero, so the support is bounded above at xi + alpha/kappa = -99 and unbounded below.

cases.name: invalid_infinity
cases.comment: Test_InvalidParameters: all three parameters positive infinity.

cases.name: invalid_zero_scale
cases.comment: Test_InvalidParameters: GeneralizedNormal(100, 0, 1) -- the scale must be strictly positive.

cases.name: product_moments_xi97_alpha35_kappa_neg01
cases.comment: Test_Moments asserts only self-consistency against CentralMoments(1E-8), so it carries no literal. These are the four product moments plus Median and Mode off the real C# GeneralizedNormal(9.7, 3.5, -0.1), the same object the CDF case above pins. The first four come from the base class's fixed 1000-step CentralMoments quadrature -- identical stepping in both ports, so the residual is rounding noise, not quadrature error, and it measures 5e-16 / 1.1e-15 / 1.7e-14 / 4.9e-15 for mean / sd / skewness / kurtosis. They are asserted at 1e-9 relative, the tier the other quadrature-moment families use, leaving headroom for the platforms CI runs. Median is the closed-form InverseCDF(0.5) and Mode the bounded BrentSearch maximiser over [InverseCDF(0.001), InverseCDF(0.999)]; both reproduce bit-for-bit against C# on this platform but are asserted at the same conventional tiers (1e-12 relative, 1e-9 absolute) rather than at equality.

cases.name: seeded_random_draws
cases.comment: Proves the inverse-CDF draw off the shared bit-exact Mersenne Twister reproduces the C# stream, and (through the R and Python fixture runners) that the same seed gives the same draw in both languages.

cases.name: quantile_gradient_xi97_alpha35_kappa_neg01
cases.comment: The IStandardError surface. Test_GNO_PartialDerivatives asserts QuantileGradient against the same NumericalDerivative.Gradient call the method makes internally, so it carries no literal; these are the real C# gradients of InverseCDF(p) with respect to {xi, alpha, kappa} at three probabilities, dumped at full precision. args are [probability, index], the flattened convention the GEV slice already speaks (whose own gradient rows sit at a loose 0.01 only because they are hand-transcribed 5-significant-figure literals, not because the method is imprecise). Both ports run the identical central-difference step rule (rel_step 1e-5 on |theta_j| + 1) over identical inputs, so the truncation error is a property of the value being pinned, not of the comparison. What the tolerance has to cover is CANCELLATION: dividing by 2h amplifies the last bits of the two InverseCDF evaluations by 1/(2h), which is 4.5e4 for kappa and 1.1e4 for alpha. Measured C++-vs-C# residual on this platform: bit-identical at p = 0.5 and p = 0.99, and 1.6e-10 absolute (6.1e-11 relative, about 2 ulp of the underlying quantile) on the p = 0.1 kappa component. 1e-8 relative is the tier that follows -- several hundred ulp of quantile headroom for a platform whose exp / inverse-normal round differently -- and is still six orders tighter than the GEV gradient rows, while any structural gradient defect (wrong index, wrong step rule, wrong sign) misses by orders of magnitude. The p = 0.5 row is structural rather than incidental: StandardZ(0.5) is exactly 0, so InverseCDF(0.5) = xi identically in alpha and kappa, the gradient there is exactly (1, 0, 0), and the two zeros are asserted absolutely. ParameterCovariance and QuantileVariance are NOT pinned: upstream GeneralizedNormal.cs (509, 515) throws NotImplementedException for both, which the port mirrors, so there is no oracle to reproduce.
